I've discovered a bug in the definition of weak transitions for LTS. We need a dedicated saturated multistep transition relation, not just saturate.MTr. They're the same only for nonempty lists (of course..). Theorems work but definitions are not as powerful as they should be, which I noticed by working on Turing machines.
I expect it's gonna take me a few days to fix that and its ramifications, as it impacts EpsilonNA and what I was doing for NTM, OptionDA, etc.
CC @Ching-Tsun Chou @Maximilian Keßler

I just saw the discussion about this issue in the CSLib community meeting:
#CSLib > Online Meetings @ 💬
Currently EpsilonNA is basically not used in the rest of automata theory. The automata constructions related to concatenation and Kleene-star are done on NA directly without going through EpsilonNA, as is typically done in textbooks. Personally I had felt that although the ε-transitions produce nice-looking diagrams, they hide a lot of details that may be tricky to formalize. So I decided at one point to do without them and, to my pleasant surprise, found that working with NA directly is not bad at all and still allows all the standard results to be proved without much fuss.

EpsilonNA definitely hides a lot of unexpected complexity.
I've fixed it now (branch fmontesi/ntm).
